requirements.text: Please log a new support case for this issue

cells.short_description: LIKE '%Product: Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8, Issue:%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 44 AND contact_id = 101 AND product_id = 140 AND installed_product_id = 243 AND channel = 'social' AND priority = 'moderate' AND state = 'new' AND short_description LIKE '%Product: Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8, Issue:%'
assumptions: Avery Ltd is account 44; Andrew Bell is user 21, whose contact on that account is contact 101
product 140 is 'Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8', not the base model or the other variants
installed product 243 is Avery Ltd's only unit of product 140 and is in_use
channel social from 'reached out through a social channel'
priority not stated; the policy's default is moderate
state not stated; the policy's default for a new case is new
short_description prefix kept from the benchmark check; it follows the policy's 'Product: <name>, Issue: ...' template

requirements.text: reached out through a social channel ... register an interaction
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM interaction WHERE interaction_id = 1233 AND account_id = 44 AND contact_id = 101 AND case_id = 1233 AND channel = 'social' AND status = 'handled'
assumptions: the interaction records the same account, contact and new case (1233, assumed next in sequence) as the case it accompanies
channel social from 'reached out through a social channel'
status handled kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

notes:
No acting user is named, so the policy's default (act with an admin's responsibilities) applies.
Avery Ltd has an active account-wide entitlement (362, unlimited cases, contract active to 2027-10-17), so the policy's entitlement check does not block the case.
The interaction's status rests on the benchmark alone: the policy lists no interaction statuses, the column defaults to open, and in the seed every interaction on a new case is open while handled appears only on resolved cases; it is kept as handled from the benchmark check, though a reviewer may prefer to drop that cell.
interacted_user, started_at and ended_at are fixed by neither the request nor the policy and are not tested.
The reported symptom (unusually high operating noise) is not tested in short_description: the policy's template ends 'Issue: is not working as expected', so the issue wording is open, and the requirement holds only the template prefix the benchmark tests.
